text: Imagine hunting with a torch your prey can't see.
In the deep sea, almost every light is blue — because blue is the light that travels best through water.
And most deep-sea animals can't see red at all.
But three kinds of loose-jawed dragonfish carry a second light, under each eye. It shines far-red — beyond seven hundred nanometres.
And unlike almost everything around them, they can see it.
So picture it: a red beam sweeping through the dark, lighting up animals that have no idea they're lit.
One of them sees its red light with a pigment you would never expect to find in a fish's eye.
What it is, and seven more tricks of the deep, is linked right here.
